# JXL Art — code-golfed cellular-automaton images (manifest)

## What this project is (read this first)

**Problem.** Produce JPEG XL (`.jxl`) images that are each **at most 1024 bytes on disk** yet at least
**1024x1024 pixels**, where the picture is *generated by the decoder itself* rather than stored.
JPEG XL's "modular" mode predicts every pixel from already-decoded neighbours using a small decision
tree (the "MA tree"). If the encoded residuals are all zero, the tree alone *is* the image. Because
each pixel's prediction can read its West/North/North-West/North-East neighbours (and the same
position in previously decoded channels), the tree acts as a **cellular automaton** run row by row,
left to right. This is what the JXL Art community does; the web tool is https://jxl-art.lucaversari.it/
(help page: https://jxl-art.lucaversari.it/wtf.html, source: https://github.com/veluca93/jxl-art).

**Deliverables (each a separate `.jxl` <= 1024 bytes, >= 1024x1024):**
1. `digits` — a grid of seven-segment **1s and 0s**, digit choice pseudo-random, generated by a chaotic CA.
2. `flag` — an **American flag** (13 stripes, blue canton, 50 five-pointed stars in the 6/5 stagger).
3. `text` — a grid of pseudo-random **ASCII characters** (glyphs rendered from a compact font),
   again with the CA choosing the characters.
4. `text_infinity` (v1) — the same text masked to an infinity symbol, whole characters only;
   `text_infinity_v2` — v1 with a green-amber CRT look (scanlines, phosphor glow).
5. `equations` — lines of random well-formed equations with matched parentheses, function
   names written downward; `equations_crt` — the same with the CRT look; `equations_v2` —
   names inline (SIN COS TAN EXP), syntax-coloured by token kind, two 60-token equations per
   row with a 12-cell gap, a blank row between lines, and equations of random length (8 to 52 tokens); `equations_v3` — the same on a
   1024x1024 single-group canvas, one 64-token equation per line.

**Hard constraints:** file size <= 1024 bytes (`anything above a kilobyte is banned`), image
>= 1024x1024, the CA must drive the randomness, every result is visually verified by Claude
looking at the decoded PNG (the "VLM check"), no agents for the first pass.

## Glossary

- **JXL Art** — the practice of hand-writing a JPEG XL modular prediction tree so that the decoder's
  predictions, with zero residual, generate an image.
- **Tree / MA tree** — the decision tree (`if property > value` nodes with predictor leaves) that JPEG
  XL modular mode evaluates per pixel. The "source code" of a piece is a `.tree` text file.
- **Predictor / leaf** — `- Name +offset`: the pixel value is the predictor's output plus the offset.
  `Set` predicts 0, so `- Set 255` means "pixel = 255". `- W +1` means "left neighbour + 1".
- **Property** — a value the tree can branch on: `x`, `y`, `c` (channel index), `g` (group id),
  neighbours `N W NW NE`, differences like `W-NW`, and `Prev`/`Prev2`/... (same pixel in an earlier
  channel). See the language reference below.
- **Channel** — one plane of the modular image. Colour channels are R,G,B. Extra planes declared with
  `HiddenChannel n` are decoded *before* RGB, are invisible in the output, and serve as CA state.
- **Cell** — a fixed-size square tile of the canvas holding one digit/glyph/star. Its local
  coordinates `xm = x mod CELL`, `ym = y mod CELL` come from **counter channels**.
- **Counter channel** — hidden channel whose value increments from its W (or N) neighbour and wraps,
  giving `x mod P` (or `y mod P`) without any modulo operator.
- **Rule 30** — the elementary CA `new = NW xor (N or NE)` run on the row above; NE and NW are
  recovered from the `N-NE` / `NW-N` properties. It is the randomness source of every piece.
  (A "skewed" rule on `NW, N, W` was tried first and is never chaotic: information only flows
  one way.)
- **Group** — JPEG XL decodes the frame in independent square groups (`128 << GroupShift`, max
  1024). Inside a group, `x`, `y`, and neighbour lookups are **group-local**: a 2048-wide image is
  two independent 1024-wide worlds that only differ in `g`. Verified empirically (see Lessons).
- **Clamping** — modular pixel values are unbounded int32 during decoding and clamped to 0..255 only
  when written to the output. Values like 300 or -50 are legal state; they display as white/black.
- **Dump** — a self-contained, portable git project directory (see "Dump protocol").
- **VLM check** — Claude decodes the `.jxl` to PNG with `djxl` and *looks at it* with its vision
  model before declaring a piece done.
- **Code golf** — minimising the byte size of the `.jxl`. The `.tree` text size is irrelevant; the
  entropy-coded tree inside the `.jxl` is what counts (baseline overhead is only ~25-40 bytes).

Claude's reading: "ASCII texts ... randomly" = a grid of pseudo-random ASCII characters (letters and/or
digits) rendered as pixel glyphs, analogous to the 1/0 grid. "WOM problems" = write-only-memory:
installs that leave no trace in the dump. Top level therefore holds `setup.sh` next to the manifest.

## Dump protocol (applies to this whole directory)

- Everything is relative to the git root; no absolute paths anywhere in the dump.
- Every system install is reproduced by top-level `setup.sh` (idempotent, macOS + Linux).
- Top level contains ONLY: `claude_instructions.md` (this file), `concerns.md`, `setup.sh`,
  `.claude_todo.md`, `.gitignore`, and the `art/` directory. All source, experiments and outputs live
  under `art/`.

## File layout

```
setup.sh                    installs jpeg-xl tools (jxl_from_tree, djxl, jxlinfo) + python deps
claude_instructions.md      this manifest
concerns.md                 append-only history of mistakes/lessons/progress
.claude_todo.md             task list mirror
art/
  build.py                  Fire CLI: compile .tree -> .jxl -> .png, print sizes, fail if > 1024 B
  trees/<name>.tree         source of each piece (readable, commented with /* */)
  out/<name>.jxl, .png      build outputs (committed: they ARE the deliverable)
  experiments/              throwaway trees and simulators used while exploring
```

## Tooling

- `jxl_from_tree in.tree out.jxl` (from Homebrew `jpeg-xl` 0.12.0) compiles a tree text to `.jxl`.
- `djxl out.jxl out.png` decodes for viewing. `jxlinfo` prints header info.
- Python: `/opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.10/bin/python3.10` on macOS (per user global rules), Fire for CLIs.

## Tree language reference (condensed from wtf.html + tools/jxl_from_tree.cc)

Tokens are whitespace separated; indentation is cosmetic; `/* ... */` comments allowed.
Header keywords (all optional, any order, before the tree): `Width n`, `Height n` (default 1024),
`Bitdepth n` (8), `RCT n` (0 = plain RGB, 6 = YCoCg), `GroupShift 0..3` (group = 128<<n, default 3),
`HiddenChannel n` (n extra invisible channels decoded first; RGB become channels n..n+2),
`Alpha`, `Orientation 0..7`, `Upsample 1|2|4|8`, `XYB`, `CbYCr`, `Squeeze`, `FramePos x y`,
`NotLast`, `Spline ... EndSpline`, `Animation`, `Duration`, `BlendMode`.

Decision node: `if <property> > <int>` followed by the THEN subtree then the ELSE subtree (pre-order).
Leaf: `- <predictor> <int>` or `- <predictor> +<int>` / `-<int>` (offset is mandatory).

Properties: `c g y x |N| |W| N W W-WW-NW+NWW W+N-NW W-NW NW-N N-NE N-NN W-WW WGH`
`Prev PrevAbs PrevErr PrevAbsErr` (= `Prev1...`), `Prev2 ... Prev19` (+`Abs`/`Err`/`AbsErr`).
Predictors: `Set W N NW NE WW Select Gradient Weighted AvgW+N AvgW+NW AvgN+NW AvgN+NE AvgAll`.

Edge rules: at x=y=0, W=0; at x=0, W=N; at y=0, N=W; at x=0 or y=0, NW=W; NE,NN fall back to N;
WW falls back to W. Decoding order: channel by channel, each channel row-major.

## Verified semantics (tested 2026-09-03 with jpeg-xl 0.12.0; see art/experiments/)

- `- Set 300` shows white, `- Set -50` shows black: values are clamped only at output.
- `HiddenChannel 1` + counter `if x > 0 [if W > 62 - Set 0 - W +1] - Set 0` gives x mod 64 in an
  invisible channel; RGB read it via `Prev`. jxlinfo reports "RGB+Optional".
- Baseline sizes: 25 B (one split), 37 B (hidden channel + counter), 47 B (4 groups, 3 splits).
- Multi-group images: `x` is group-local (a 2048-wide image never sees `x > 1500`) and neighbour
  propagation restarts at group boundaries. Use `g` to tell groups apart.

## Design (per piece) — current state, sizes as of 2026-09-03

### The randomness engine (shared by digits and text)
Rule 30 (`new = NW xor (N or NE)`) in a hidden channel, run row by row over the whole canvas.
- NW and NE are not properties; with N known they are recovered from `NW-N` and `N-NE`.
- "on" is encoded as 100, "off" as 0, so thresholds are 49 / -51 / -50 everywhere.
- Seed row 0 = Weyl sequence `v = (v + 633) mod 1024` (period > width: a periodic seed would
  stay periodic forever because the CA is translation invariant). Row 1 thresholds it at 511.
- Column 0 = Weyl sequence `(v + 37) mod 100` running downward. Rule 30 carries information
  rightward at speed 1 but leftward only weakly, so a constant left boundary makes the first
  columns periodic in y (observed period 64). The boundary sequence injects entropy.
- Cells sample the CA a few pixels inside the cell (digits: xm=8, ym=7) or several rows below
  the seed (text: rows 7..11) so boundary/seed structure does not show.

### digits (1/0 grid) — art/trees/digits.tree, 177 B
`HiddenChannel 4`: c0 xm = x mod 64, c1 ym = y mod 64, c2 Rule 30, c3 = cell bit (sampled at
(xm=8, ym=7), copied right with W and down with N), c4 R = seven-segment glyph (cell 64, glyph
box xm 16..47, ym 8..55, stroke 6, 1 px gaps; "0" = a b c d e f, "1" = b c), c5/c6 copy R.

### flag — art/trees/flag.tree, 223 B (v1 in art/experiments/flag_v1.tree, 261 B)
Canvas 1946x1024 (10:19), 13 stripes of 79 px, canton 780x553 limited to group g=21, stripes from
`ys = y mod 158` only. Star lattice: `ym = (y+27) mod 55` (row pitch 55), `U = xm - 65` counter
over -65..64 whose row start alternates between -65 and 0 each time ym wraps (the 6/5 stagger),
star centre (u=0, ym=30), R = 30. Star membership from three hidden linear channels built by
propagation (`N +- b` down a column, `W +- 3` along a row, sign flip at u = 0 gives 3|u|):
`L2 = ym - 3|u|`, `L4 = 167 - 3|u| - 4ym`, `L5 = 167 + 3|u| - 4ym`, plus `L1 = ym > 20`:
`star = (L4 & L2) | (L4 & !L2 & L1) | (!L4 & L1 & L2 & L5)` (13 nodes). R holds the region
colour directly (255 white / 178 red / 60 blue); G and B are derived from R by two thresholds.
Colours: white, Old Glory red (178,34,52), Old Glory blue (60,59,110).

### text — art/trees/text.tree (346 B, 1024x1024) and text_infinity.tree (524 B, 2048x1024), GENERATED by art/gen_text_tree.py
Regenerate with `python3.10 art/gen_text_tree.py` and
`python3.10 art/gen_text_tree.py --mask lemniscate --name text_infinity` (add `--charset16` for a
16-letter variant that saves ~85 B).
Edit the generator, never the .tree files. The generator is a tiny tree DSL (`If`, `Leaf`, `Set`,
`chain`, `runs_tree`, `dispatch`) plus one function per channel, so nothing is pasted twice.
- Cells 16x32; ONE hidden counter `cc = 32*xm + ym` (both cell coordinates are thresholds on
  one value: `xm > k` <=> `cc > 32k+31`; `ym > k` inside a known column <=> `cc > 32xm + k`).
  Bands start at y = 20; the first band is blanked (2 nodes) so the first drawn line samples the
  CA 60 steps below the seed row: a Weyl seed sampled every 16 px always has a near-return with
  ~3% differing bits at some distance <= 63 cells (pigeonhole), and 28 steps left visible echoes.
  `Orientation 4` flips the image so the spare 64 px margin is at the bottom; the font is
  emitted upside down in decode space (`decoded_glyph`) so letters display upright.
- A = Rule 30 with on = 1024; row 0 and column 0 are Weyl sequences (v+633) mod 1024 whose raw
  values feed the rule through the same "> 511" thresholds (no separate threshold row).
- V = character value assembled in column xm == 1 from consecutive CA rows (`Set 2^(b-1)` then
  `N + 2^k`). There is NO blank glyph (user: "space should not be one of the characters"); a
  blank cell is a negative V (the pattern channel emits 0 for `V <= -1`). With a mask, the last
  bit's update is gated by `|S| <= half-width` (`PrevAbs` on a centred field), so a cell outside
  becomes blank as a whole.
- P = the current glyph row's 3-bit pattern: at xm == 2 a run-length tree per glyph row maps V to
  the pattern; copied right with W; at glyph columns 1 and 2 the consumed high bit is subtracted
  (`if W > 3: W - 4`, `if W > 1: W - 2`) so R lights a pixel with a single threshold (3, 1, 0).
  Encoding rows instead of pixels shares bit changes that happen together (32 glyphs: 361 -> 325 B).
- Glyph set: both pieces use all 32 glyphs A-Z + `! ? . , { }` (user: "does it even use all the
  letters and !.{} etc"). The 16-letter set "ABDEFHIKNOPRTVXY" (local search, keeps A E I O,
  art/experiments/charset_search.py) is available with `--charset16` and saves ~85 B.
  Character order comes from random-restart 2-opt on the row-pattern Hamming distance.
- text_infinity is 2048x1024 (user: "bigger ... fit the aspect ratio ... more letters and not
  square"). That is two decoder groups with group-local x, so the seed row (different Weyl step
  per group, else the halves would be copies) and the mask field branch on `g` (21 left, 22 right).
- R draws; G and B are `Set 0` deltas under `RCT 3` (G += R, B += R), i.e. greyscale.

Mask (only whole characters are ever drawn — the field is tested once per cell at its sample
point): channels cannot be added, so a mask field must be separable, S = f(x) + g(y). Two
overlapping rings cross at a shallow angle (a lens, user: "should look like an X"), so the
shipped `lemniscate` mask is a genuine figure-eight: Gerono's y^2 = x^2 - x^4/a^2 generalised to
S = (|u|^p / a^(p-2) - u^2 + k v^2) / 16 with p = 3.5, a = 0.44 W, k = 1.4 (vertical squash), and
the band -eps < S <= eps, eps = 100000 px^2, centred so membership is one `|S| <= half-width`
test via `PrevAbs`. A level-set band bulges where the gradient vanishes, so the crossing came
out as a blob ("gloopy"). Fix: a second linear field L = den|v| - num|u| (num/den = 5/8, also
separable, +-5/+-8 steps) draws the crossing as two straight strokes of constant width: within
|u| < 0.22 W a cell is drawn iff |L| <= w, beyond that iff |S| <= half-width. The line and w are
fitted so the straight stroke passes through the centre of the polynomial band at the reach and
has the same height there (no seam). p = 3.5 balances tip thickness against hole size (p = 4 has
thin tips, p = 3 closes the holes at the same boldness). Predictors are linear, so the polynomials
are grown by rounded chord slopes over 128-px pieces aligned to the centre (exact at breakpoints,
a few px off between). The crossing sits on the group boundary of the 2048-wide canvas: the left
group holds u in [-1024, 0), the right u in [0, 1024) (one chain each). ~120 nodes for S + L.
Tried and dropped (see concerns.md): diamond / clipped-hexagon rings ("looks like the HSBC
logo"), knee-slope hexagons, elliptical rings ("2 circles next to each other").

### text_infinity_v2 — CRT look (602 B), `--crt`
Same text and mask as v1 plus two hidden channels and a colour rule (all in art/gen_text_tree.py):
- `sl` = y mod 4; rows with sl == 0 are darkened (x0.55) in letters and background alike.
- `C` glow class: 3 on lit glyph pixels, else W - 1 (a phosphor trail fading to the right over
  2 px: levels 2, 1), and 2 on the pixel before a lit glyph column. This needs the pattern
  channel to compute the pattern one pixel early and peel a bit on the LAST pixel of each column
  (`pattern_channel(..., early=1)`), so on that pixel "lit" is `W > 2` and the pattern's top bit
  already belongs to the next column. A symmetric halo would need the next cell's value or a
  second font lookup (~+80 B); the one-sided trail is ~5 B and matches beam direction.
- `R` = brightness table (class x scanline: 4 x 2 leaves), G = R + 25 and B = R - 255 via RCT 3
  (`Set` constants), so bright pixels are amber-yellow (215,240,0), dim ones green, background
  (8,33,0).
- A superellipse tube field with three vignette bands and black corners was built and removed
  (user: "not smooth and seems to have added a lot of bytes"; it cost ~130 B). Smooth vignettes
  are not available: brightness can only take a few discrete leaf values per region.

### equations — equations.tree (556 B), equations_crt.tree (625 B), equations_v2.tree (705 B), equations_v3.tree (652 B), equations_v4.tree (840 B)
Generate with `--equations`, `--equations --crt`, `--equations --inline --gap 12 --row_gap 1 --random_length` (v2) and
`--equations --inline --width 1024 --name equations_v3` (v3) and
`--equations --inline --gap 12 --row_gap 1 --random_length --one_equals --tall_parens --width 4096 --height 2048 --name equations_v4` (v4).
A context-free grammar rendered as text. Matched parentheses of one kind are a one-counter
language (Dyck-1), so no stack is needed: tokens are generated left to right, one per 16x32 cell,
by a counter automaton whose whole state is one channel value `S = 8*class + depth` (classes
OPEN, OP, FUNC, CLOSE, OPERAND, BLANK; depth 0..3). The class is a threshold band and every
transition is `W + constant`, so the decision tree is not duplicated per depth (~45 nodes).
Grammar: `E -> operand | ( E ) | fn ( E ) | E op E`, operands Y Z 1 2 3, operators + - · / ^
(= only at depth 0; multiplication is a centred dot, user: "use a dot not a *"), fn SIN COS TAN
EXP. `(` requires depth < 3 and room, `)` requires depth > 0, and the last cells of a line force
closes (`x` thresholds, each decoder group is a 64-cell line), so every line balances. Random
choices use the 5-bit value V. The first band is blank (too close to the seed row).
- v1 (`equations`): classes OPEN OP FUNC CLOSE OPERAND BLANK; RT row type 0/1/2 cycles per cell
  band; function names hang downward: the token channel in hanging rows copies the successor
  letter of the glyph above (S->I->N etc.). Not flipped. 10 lines per group.
- v2 (`equations_v2`, user: "sin and tan inline", "syntax-highlight"): classes OPEN OP FN1 FN2
  FN3 CLOSE OPERAND BLANK; a name is three consecutive states and the token channel copies the
  successor letter of the glyph to the LEFT (its xm == 0 column copies W for that; row 0 is
  blank so the copy chains start blank). Every cell row is a line (30 per group). Colour:
  channel K = 0 unlit else 1 + kind of the glyph (parens, operators, variables, digits,
  functions; the glyph order keeps kinds contiguous so kind = thresholds on the token), and
  R G B are five-entry palette lookups (EQ_PALETTE), no RCT. `gap` cells at the end of each
  group stay blank (v2: up to 52-token equations, 12-cell gap between the two per row); `row_gap`
  blank cell rows between lines are made by a row-type channel RT (period row_gap + 1) that
  blanks the state on spacer rows (v2: 1, so 15 lines per group). `random_length` lets the state go
  BLANK after any top-level operand once EQ_MIN_CELLS (8) tokens are drawn when V > EQ_END_V (23,
  1 in 4), so lengths are geometric from 8 up to the forced-close cap at the line width; every
  equation still ends well formed because ending is only offered at depth 0 after an operand. Gap sizes change only
  threshold constants, so the byte count is unchanged.
- v3 (`equations_v3`, user: "one equation per line"): v2 on a 1024x1024 canvas. One decoder
  group means one line per cell row; a line cannot span two groups because groups decode
  independently and the depth counter cannot cross the boundary.
Verification: `python3.10 art/experiments/verify_equations.py equations|equations_v2` reads the
glyphs back from the PNG (max of R,G,B > 60 = lit) and checks every line: 20/20, 30/30, 30/30.
- v4 (`equations_v4`, user: "not all lines hace exactly one = now" ... "make that a  neww version.
  also can we make outer parentheis bigger and bigger"): v2's layout (gap 12, row_gap 1, random
  length) plus `one_equals` and `tall_parens`.
  `one_equals`: S = 8*class + 2*depth + a, a = 1 once the "=" has been written. "=" is offered
  (V > EQ_EQUALS_V, 1 in 2) only at depth 0 before it and ending only after it; the forced-close
  zone starts two cells earlier (and functions need one more cell) so "=" plus an operand always
  fit. The "=" state is the OPEN class at depth 0 (a real "(" has depth >= 1), so the token
  channel draws it from the OPEN band with one extra split; "=" leaves the operator pool.
  `tall_parens`: opens are drawn {, [, ( by depth after opening 1..3 and closers }, ], ) by depth
  after closing 0..2 (six paren glyphs, order "{[()]}" so their bars share runs). Heights 13, 9, 5
  glyph rows (52, 36, 20 px) centred on the text: the cap rows are 010, the bars 100 / 001. Two
  bands per line, a 24-glyph-row frame: the odd band (RT 1) decides tokens at row 19 (V sampled
  rows 15..19) and draws frame rows 5..7 below that; the even band (RT 0) copies S and T down and
  draws frame rows 8..15 with the text at 9..13; the next odd band still holds the previous
  tokens above its decision row and draws frame rows 16..19 there. Nothing can be drawn above the
  decision row (pixels there are decoded before the token exists), which is why the decision sits
  low in the odd band. P = tall_pattern_channel (frame per token from tall_frame), row cases only
  where the frame row changes. First decide band is band 1 (samples at rows 67..71); 15 lines per
  group; the verifier reads the even bands with the text at band row 4 and requires one "=".
  Canvas 4096x2048 (user: "plz make it 4k"): 4x2 decoder groups, each a fresh 1024x1024 tile of the
  same layout (x, y, the counters and the CA seeds are all group-local), 120 equations. 3840x2160
  was rejected: a 768-px group column has no room for the x-threshold forced closes (equations would
  run off the group edge) and a 112-px group row would clip the last line's parens. Seeds: with more
  than two groups every group k starts its Weyl seed row SEED_SHIFT * k values further along the
  sequence (a chain over g, ids 21.. in raster order; 4096x2048 has 21..24 over 25..28); the shift is odd so no group samples the same
  Rule 30 columns as another. Eight groups cost ~15 B of TOC over two.

### Decoder validity: no redundant splits
libjxl validates trees on decode: a split on a property whose outcome is already fixed by an
ancestor split on the same property (e.g. `x > 928` inside the else branch of `x > 928`) makes
the file encode fine but FAIL TO DECODE ("Failed to decode image"). The DSL's `simplify()` pass
removes such splits from every generated tree; hand-written trees must avoid them.

### Byte-cost model (measured)
Baseline ~25 B; **each hidden channel costs 6 B of header**; repetitive trees cost ~1.2 B/node,
diverse ones ~2 B/node. Golfing = fewer channels, fewer *distinct* properties/split values/
offsets, then fewer nodes. Node removals inside an already-repetitive tree often save nothing.

## Verification strategy

1. `python3.10 art/build.py` compiles every `art/trees/*.tree`, prints byte sizes, and errors on
   any `.jxl` > 1024 bytes.
2. Claude reads every `art/out/*.png` (VLM check) and records the assessment in concerns.md.
3. Numeric checks where visual inspection is weak: decode to PNG, load with Pillow, and assert cell
   statistics (e.g. digit density between 30% and 70%, no two identical rows of cells).

## Success criteria

- Ten `.jxl` files in `art/out/` (digits 177 B, flag 222 B, text 346 B, text_infinity 524 B, text_infinity_v2 602 B, equations 556 B, equations_crt 625 B, equations_v2 705 B, equations_v3 652 B (1024x1024), equations_v4 840 B (4096x2048) (4096x2048); six of them at 2048x1024, v4 at 4096x2048), each <= 1024 bytes, each >= 1024 px on the short side, each visually correct. (The user's 300 B target for the infinity text was met at 299 B in the square 16-letter hexagon version; the wide canvas, true lemniscate and full 32-glyph set they asked for afterwards cost ~170 B more; `--charset16` saves ~85 B.)
- The random choices come from a CA inside the tree, not from a stored table.
- Fresh session can rebuild everything with `./setup.sh && python3.10 art/build.py`.

## Lessons learned (never remove; add only)

- 2026-09-03: Homebrew jpeg-xl bottle was linked against a removed imath dylib; `brew reinstall
  jpeg-xl` fixes it. Any such install must be in `setup.sh` (dump protocol) *at the time it is done*.
- 2026-09-03: `x`/`y` and neighbours are group-local; do not rely on global coordinates beyond 1024.
- 2026-09-03: Leaf nodes require an explicit offset token (`- N 0`), or the parser fails.
